The good news is that it's an early access game that works, both technically and as an idea. I can see the fun to be had, but I do have some input. If you're looking for a challenge game that forces you to learn, this is solid. If you want some help with learning from your mistakes, this really isn't the game for you. But it could be. Like a few of the negative reviews I've read, I do think there is a conversation to be had about the base difficulty, which is the only way I can play because I can't for the life of me unlock anything higher. The default mode for someone like me (who's trying to learn without looking down much) is somewhat unforgiving, even with some of the assistant perks I've earned. It also does little as a teaching tool, with nothing in the way of feedback other than the number of mistakes you're making. I've got a short list of suggestions: - The boss sections. It feels like I'm just continuing the level with this big thing at the top of my screen, and I'm scrambling to defeat harder and harder base enemies instead of using my levels I'm earning to create more space for myself to focus on the boss text. This kind of design would work great in a normal game, but in a learning experience it prevents any feeling of success, which doesn't feel great. Not being able to beat even the first trial is demoralizing. - Tell me what I'm doing wrong. I feel like even by myself, I can tell that there's certain keys I'm whiffing. If I'm working though words and constantly missing a key, tell me about it after I lose. Maybe even offer some kind of practice level where that key shows up a lot. - A system to keep track of those problems I'm having. Some kind of player profile that shows me how I may be growing outside of what I've unlocked. "You used to miss the "Y" key this much, and now it's only this much." Something like that maybe? - Prioritize the text or space out the enemies. After a while, the enemies overlap each others text, meaning I can't see one or more of the things I need to type. Add in my various weapons all over the screen, and finding the words becomes an issue. A very frustrating issue once things begin to heat up. I switched to dark mode to try and alleviate the problem, but that didn't help. - Jam the gun. Okay, this might sound contradictory to me complaining about the difficulty, but what if, when you mess up, you had to hit the backspace to "clear the jam" of your main weapon? Just a fun little idea, maybe an optional thing or something only on higher difficulties. - Tell me my WPM. If you can see it, why not let me know what my best/worst/average was? % of correct vs. incorrect is great, but there could be a lot more on that results screen. If I'm being honest, the biggest issue for me is the clutter preventing me from seeing all of the words I need to see. If that gets ruled out I can change it to a thumbs up and do my best to get over the difficulty... but it would be nice to clear a few levels out of the gate. I think as far as the bullet hell mechanics go, it's very well done so far. Best of luck in your continued development! Edit (late Dec 2024): I personally haven't seen many of the issues I talked about addressed, and all previously mentioned problems still hold true. In fact, I noticed that now even more than before, enemies like to hide behind the giant boss text during the boss segment, and while they're back there it's impossible to see them or their text. The enemies are still growing harder and harder as this segment goes on, which means I don't see myself clearing trial 1 anytime soon unless I get really lucky and the enemies remain visible. I do feel as if the earlier parts of the level were easier, but this is double sided: less enemies earlier in the level, less levels and upgrades I have once the boss shows up. Before I could even get through 50% of the boss text I was being swarmed. Still a thumbs down from me, but I'm looking forward to future updates.

It's to much. I bought the game under the assumption that it'd be a good relaxing game, it's not. There's simply way to much going on at the same time for it to be enjoyable I feel, let me try and paint you a picture because the video on display is not a good indicator. - Typing. First and foremost, the way you control the game is through typing, practically nothing will happen without you typing. You will not reach a point where the upgrades take over and you can relax. It's what we signed on for and that is fine, but keep this fact in mind when reading on, you are constantly typing while dealing with everything else. - Enemy variety, a stable of any game, some targets are higher priority than others. The enemies does different things, some spawn more enemies, some are very fast, some have rotating shields, etc. etc. There are a lot of enemy types, which is usually great, but there is a lot, even in the very first map. But it complicates targeting priority, which is fine on it's own. - Secondary weapons, when you type the name of an enemy, you fire your Primary weapon at that enemy. But Secondary weapons are only fired under specific conditions, a few are automatic, but most have requirements. Usually the requirement is to type out a word starting with one of four specific letters. The words are connected to the enemies, the enemies are not all the same, so now you have to prioritise not only the enemies but also factor in which words is simply more valuable, because they fire your secondary weapons. This complicates target priority even more. - Horde, as the description rightly states, it's a horde survival game. There will be a lot of enemies on the screen at the same time, which complicates target priority even further. Not only are some enemies more dangerous, some words more valuable, but you also have to factor in clusters of enemies and which words will actually deal with them, because your primary weapon is not an area attack. - Pick Ups, occasionally the enemies will drop items for you to pick up. Healing, extra upgrades, shields negating a single damage instance, rerolls, double damage and screen freeze. That's all great, but picking up these boons requires you to type out their corresponding word. Keystrokes you could be using to thin the horde. - Combo, typing words correctly will net you a combo bonus in the form of critical chance. A single wrong keystroke and the bonus is lost and the word you were typing is reset, same word but you must start over. So while you're dealing with everything above, you are punished heavily for singular mistakes. - Dead enemies, didn't expect this one did you? Dead enemies are a problem too. A lot of your secondary weapons don't kill the enemies immediately, so you also have to keep track of where your mines and drones are going, because you don't want to waste time on something they are already going to kill, that's keystrokes wasted, especially if your target dies as you're typing out its word. - The words, I can appreciate that I might not know every word in the english dictionary, it's not my first language after all. But there are a lot of odd and obscure words used in this and not much rhyme or reason to them. Slap this on top of everything else, you'll be dealing with strange words that you may not even know how to spell, causing you to look to and from the screen, some of them are fairly long too considering you're meant to type it out in the middle of a horde. - Boss, now to top it all off, the boss. After playing for 4 minutes the boss spawns, it doesn't technically do anything, however... The way you deal with the boss is that in the middle of the screen you'll have snippet of a text, as you type the letters you'll progress through the text, mistyping will not reset the text but will still cost you the combo bonus. The text is presumably about 80 words long. The regular enemies does not stop spawning, in fact they continue to escalate. More and more enemies of more and more powerful types. On top of all that typing and prioritisation I've outlined, you now also have to somehow find space to chip away at the boss' blurb of text. I hope I've properly communicated just how much is going on at all times. You have to consider enemy types, enemy density, word value, enemy health, friendly weapons, pick ups, word difficulty and boss progress. All the while typing and being severely punished for missing single keystrokes. The cherry on top: I never made it past the default difficulty of the very first level, everything I've told you is from the very first level. I'm not entirely new to this way of playing either, I played and enjoyed Nanotales quite a bit, which is extremely similar in terms of gameplay. But Glyphica is stressful and extremely difficult. That's the difficulty/stress level covered my main gripe with the game. Then some minor points to round out the review: - Upgrades, they don't feel very impactful. When a drone deals 5-6 damage, increasing that damage by 10% feels really lackluster. Or giving singular weapons 1-3% chance to inflict Damage over Time, it really doesn't feel worthwhile. There are some decent ones here and there, but it really feels like the "Uncommon" powerlevel should be the baseline for "Common" upgrades. - Meta progression, I looked it over and got a few of the upgrades, but there was nothing that really stood out to me and particularly interesting. Your meta progression involves buying certain upgrades with currency collected in game and then bringing 2 upgrades along on future runs (more on higher difficulty). These upgrades included things such as "+20% HP", "+20% damage for 20sec after using a reroll" and "Speed upgrades for drones also apply to their damage". Last one was the most interesting of the bunch but rule of thumb is that the upgrades are nice to have and dictates your build, but doesn't really elevate it significantly. - Style, I actually quite like the clean aesthetic of Glyphica. Everything is sleeks and easy to see, no trouble reading the text or see what's going on. It's kind of beautiful in its simplicity. Shame I'm to busy reading and writing to actually appreciate it. I really like the concept of Glyphica and wish it was better than it currently is, it's early access so hopefully it's changed for the better before declared ready for release. As it stands, I will not recommend the game, it's simply not much fun to deal with constant, complicated decision-making while accurate working the entire keyboard, not as the base difficulty.

[h1] 【BUG】 [/h1] 游戏是好游戏但是中文版拼音打字里的[h3] ü[/h3]应该在键盘里输入[h3] v[/h3]， 而在游戏中输入v会判定是[b] 错误的输入[/b]这点很影响游戏体验。而且会担心一直玩这个游戏不知不觉以后都不会打u和v了。希望可以改进！！ ————————————————二编 首先感谢开发者对这个游戏的热情和对玩家的重视程度！！其次我在发评测的时候写的ü和v完全替代这件事情是略有偏颇的。经查询汉语拼音方案后发现，[u][b]ü和v并不完全替代[/b][/u]。目前的汉语拼音规则是ü上两点可以省略的情况下可以打作u，而ü上两点不可省略的时候则打作v。以下是参考：“(2)与ü及撮口呼韵母可以相拼的声母绝大多数是j、q、x，但u不能和j、q、x相拼，ü上两点可省略，不会与u相混。如：ju、jue、juan、jun，qu、que、quan、qun，xu、xue、xuan、xun。(3)ü、u共同可拼的声母只有n、l，ü上两点不能省略。如：nu(奴)、lu(路)；nü(女)、lü(吕)、nüe(虐)、lüe(略)。” 再次感谢开发者对于玩家留言的重视程度。祝好！

我很难说这是一个合格的“打字训练软件”，更难说这是一款合格的“肉鸽游戏”。就如同在高中时的一些同学，他们既没有完全摆烂逃课，又没有真的努力刻苦，所以最终选择了在班上最后一排偷偷拿个IPAD看美剧，一方面假装自己在学英文，另一方面又放松的不彻底。 我完全不认为一个英文或者拼音满屏幕乱飞的游戏能够帮助你练习打字，或者学习一门语言。高速的游戏流程让你不可能有额外的精力和时间去思考字符到底是什么意思；字符的大小和颜色再加上乱飞的线条，导致可视度非常不好；没有标点符号是完全和现实打字场景脱节的。 作为肉鸽游戏那就更不用提了，难度曲线不合理，流派之间不平衡，词库单一，优化欠佳，UI不合理，内容过少，引导过少等问题基本上全部都有。虽然局外成长并非肉鸽的必要因素，但是在以上问题都存在的情况下，局外成长非常慢且两个槽位能带来的提升过少，所以最后连纯爽这最后一丝挽留玩家的方面都做不到。 总的来说，可能“打字练习软件”和“肉鸽游戏”的结合本质上就有着不小的矛盾。想要练习打字不推荐，想要玩肉鸽游戏也不推荐，想要通过“看美剧学英语”的，可以试试。 [b]- 4 / 10[/b]

There's challenge, and then there's pointless grind and obnoxious bosses that will kill you no matter how fast you are, unless you have very specific upgrades to give you a fighting chance. And even then, it's all about how many specific items you get dropped; [i]nothing[/i] else matters. The upgrades and synergies are as generic as you can imagine, and "rare" items are all a joke except for one, so it's all about saving rerolls to increase the chances. Essentially, the same is one giant slot machine, which is expected given that this comes from a guy in China. What was I expecting? At least let me fight the bosses without having to sleep through the first 10 minutes of nothing happening, typing one four-letter word per second from the edge of the screen. Also it would be great if I could see the [i]rest[/i] of the game without playing the same level 20 times. Since, you know, you made it and I bought it and all that.

It's a neat game with a cool concept, but I feel like it is being held back by it's own mechanics. For starters, the normal difficulty feels quite hard, with the boss spawning in too soon without having too many upgrades to deal with the regular enemies, it just overwhelms you with sheer numbers. So maybe you could decrease the number of enemies that spawn, or better yet, remove all enemies while the boss is on screen, since it should be the main enemy you will focus on anyway. I must concede, that I do not type very fast, maybe around 40 words per minute, but jumping from word to word really slows my typing speed down to like 10 words per minute because I have to read each word that is moving towards me. It doesn't help that sometimes the words overlap with each other, making it just impossible to tell what it is. Another issue I have is my upgrades killing the enemy I'm typing, which is frustrating cause my focus is lost and I have to refocus onto a new target, which is just mentally draining. I honestly don't know how you would go about actually beating some of the waves, without being a typing god. Secondly, some upgrades just don't feel like they have the same impact as others, such as the critical chance increase or freeze drop rate increases. I often go for upgrades that aren't my main weapon, resulting in pitiful damage when I type later into the rounds, so it feels punishing to type. A suggestion I thought of is to make the primary weapon just instantly kill the enemy you type, so that you don't have to waste upgrades on the main turret damage, and can focus more on the cooler upgrades you can get for it. Which leads to the next issue, the evolution kills, if you are very good at typing fast, it feels like the evolution upgrades are slow to get, cause you are stealing kills for your main weapon. So maybe make the main weapon kills count towards all the other upgrade evolutions, which can lead to more weapon upgrade variety. Thirdly, I would like to see a game mode for when you just want to chill and type. Sometimes, I just want to relax and enjoy the unique game mechanics the game has to offer, without having to stress about efficiency all the time. A mode where you can't die, but can still obtain upgrades and coins would be nice. Or maybe less enemies spawn in and none of the annoying special enemy types like the shields. Lastly, I have only played this game for a bit, so I may have missed some options in the game. So I apologise in advance if what I have suggested is in the game already. Overall, this game has a lot of potential to be an amazing game, and I hope that the developers continue improving it.

Way too much clutter on the screen - flashing icons to press because there is an evolution or level up. This happens like 10 times per minute. - freaking amount of effects due to different upgrades (that's the game, so I could deal with that, but not the result that the words you need to type are covered). Most of the times I knew what to type because nothing else makes sense. - Words cover each other without any chance of typing the correct one. Imagine a "d" or "b" is covering a "o" And my personal favorite. Stupid-ass mechanic: If you are used to typing really fast, you are also used to hitting SPACE after every word you type... this comes as common as breathing to me. Hitting space even once, will reset the streak. So I disabled SPACE in my Logitech GHub for my Keyboard. So you should rather change the name to "Glyphica button smashing in an illogical way" Sorry for the bad review, but I can't deal with this ♥♥♥♥. I am freaking bad at designing things. Usually my games are 100% efficiency but 0% beauty building. But I wouldn't offer such a mess on my worst day. My native language is German, and I used the German template for my run. Usually I can reach around 600-650 characters a minute with 1-2 mistakes in my worst runs using Type10 or similar apps. Requested a refund anyway... so don't bother addressing those on my account. There is no 2nd chance for a 1st impression, you know. A serious question at last: Have you ever REALLY played your own game? If so, HOW CAN YOU NOT NOTICE ANY OF THE ABOVE?! Until you gave me a better explanation I maintain that you did not programm this yourself. No way! This is either AI-made or copied and you don't know how to fix those. Release date on steam: Oct. 2024 ... 1.5 years? Really?

Every process in you computer will just hang for 8-10 seconds before actually updating it's state. Cannot recommend, as I have to assume, barring the possibility that it's some specific and unique problem with my particular setup, that it will cause similar problems for anyone. Which is too bad - basic functionality, the game is a great deal of fun in the typing genre.

[h1]7/10[/h1] 给到不推荐，[u]并非是这个游戏不好玩，而是我觉得它可以更好玩[/u]。因为制作者用了顶级的创意，却做出了一个令人失望的游戏。或者与其说本作是一款游戏，不如说是游戏化教育的速打练习软件，它的受众是那些希望在练习打字的同时“找点乐子”的人，而非那些想玩游戏，被打字肉鸽的噱头吸引来的人。 本作依托类幸存者的基本玩法，使玩家通过打字来攻击不断迫近的怪群，击败一定数量的敌人后会获得升级，在3个强化buff中选择一个获得。玩家的战力则由主武器+至多四种副武器组成，当玩家完成敌人对应的词语拼写时，主武器会对该敌人进行一次攻击，当完成副武器对应条件的拼写（如完成拼写b/c/d开头的词汇），则触发一次副武器对应的效果。武器系统设计较为合理，不同武器区分度较高，但不同武器间平衡性较差。同时，游戏简约的画风清爽大气，干净的音效配合键盘有节奏的响声强化了玩家在打字中获得的快感。 如此看来，本作的创意孵化与整体框架的设计非常优秀，这也是最初我被本作吸引并进行游玩的原因，但游玩几局过后，作为一个肉鸽游戏玩家而非打字练习者，我确实发现了一些令我无法忍受的细节问题，这里仅从两个角度分析下本作所存在的问题，同时大概能够回答为什么我觉得本作比起游戏，更像是一款游戏化的打字练习器。 [h2]1.游戏有些过于依赖打字，没有发挥出肉鸽游戏的优势。[/h2] [i]在二零二六年，基本上80%的独立游戏制作者都在制作肉鸽游戏，或者往自己的游戏中添加肉鸽要素。但或许他们按需要思考一下，为什么要添加肉鸽要素，而不是看到别人拿其他玩法缝肉鸽然后火了，抱着我这么干是不是也可以的心态，照猫画虎似的向游戏里硬塞肉鸽要素。画虎画皮难画骨，他们根本不知道那些名震一时的肉鸽游戏为什么成功，为什么拿着相同框架制作出来的游戏，为什么一些会一炮而红，有些则石沉大海。[/i] 我曾不止一次在评测中强调：[b]肉鸽游戏的精髓在于超乎玩家想象的构筑，以及与之相生相伴的随机性。[/b]尤其是在肉鸽游戏设计逐渐成熟的大背景下，稍微有些游戏阅历的玩家都不会再单纯地被随机性带来的成瘾式设计所吸引，我们会仔细地审视游戏随机带来的成型难度；衡量每个选项能够带来的上限；思考不同技能之间能够产生的联动效果，同时，我们希望游戏机制能够为随机性下限保留容错；期盼游戏能在构筑质变时感受到难度曲线的骤然变化； 同时渴望在局外成长与游戏理解加深的双重作用下快速变强，在突破关卡、挑战新难度的过程中浸入心流。 虽然打字+肉鸽是一个相当有创意的玩法组合，但打字玩法与肉鸽设计有一种天生的矛盾感，因为打字本身是一件“很难以提升”的事情，尤其是对于许多不经常使用26键输入的人而言，从2字符/s到4字符/s的有效输入可能就需要几十上百个小时的练习，这恰恰与肉鸽短频快的游戏节奏与快速成长逻辑相悖。因此对难度与细节的考量便成为了“缝合”两种玩法，吸引玩家且留存玩家的核心。 然而本作似乎没有意识到这一点，或者在发现后却傲慢的为游戏设置了[i]准入门槛[/i]。除了两个不解锁成就的“休闲模式”外，通关最基础的关卡都对玩家有着较高的要求。游戏几乎所有武器的出伤均是以打字为基础来完成的，哪怕主武器强化次数再多，攻击模式也不会有太大变化，依旧是打一次字开一炮（部分主武器有增加攻击模组的进化，但依旧需要打字来触发），而副武器在生成后虽然可以在持续时间内自动出伤，但生成副武器本身仍然需要完成打字。也就是说对大多数主武器而言，无论如何“解放双手”都是不可能的，再厉害的肉鸽高手来了，也要把键盘擦出火星子。 其次，游戏的防御段与下限应对机制聊胜于无。我相信几乎所有没有专门练习过打字的人都会在平时不自觉地依赖输入法的矫正功能，并且会在游玩本作时原形毕露，错打和漏打层出不穷。在本作中，错打和漏打虽然没有惩罚，但在高压的幸存者玩法中，我们可以显而易见地得到： [b]错打=耽误一次词汇输入时间+失去一次主武器攻击机会+无法获得副武器+无法获得道具掉落等其他特效+连击奖励消失[/b] 而一次错打之后我们往往很难调整状态重新输入，恭候多时的敌人就在这一刻趁虚而入，次数盾和基础300的血量在我们的手忙脚乱中显得杯水车薪，一步错步步错，往往只是一次错打，所带来的却是摧枯拉朽的全线崩溃。在幸存者游戏中，玩家总是渴望险象环生，在死亡的边缘舞蹈来获得爽感，但在本作中我们失误之后无力回天，面对崩盘束手无策，随即满盘皆输，这种保护机制的缺失极大的加深了下限带来的挫败感，使玩家在反复受挫后放弃游玩。 这个问题是容易解决的，甚至“前辈们”也给出了许多实用的设计以供参考。例如血量下降时清屏的“分段保护”机制，就像《PVZ》中的小推车，抑或是《极简塔防》中基地受到攻击后释放的震荡波，分段保护能防止玩家“轻易的输掉游戏”，带给玩家紧迫感的同时留下一丝回旋余地。再例如主动技能的获取与使用，在肉鸽选项中加入一些带有CD的主动技能也是一个不错的选择，使玩家通过打字来释放一些强力的主动技能“解一时之急”，同样可以在解决问题的同时加强游戏的博弈性。《王国保卫战》就选择了这种方式，以火球释放、布兵、英雄系统等诸多补充机制大大增强了玩家的可玩性。 再次，敌人方面。我承认本作在敌人的设计上颇有新意，许多敌人都让人眼前一亮，比如四合一的敌人以及会为周围的友方增加buff，需要优先击杀的敌人等，以及谜语人、诗人等boss设计想法都很好。但我几乎能够肯定制作者没有做过针对一般玩家的用户调研，导致了三个明明很容易发现的问题： 1.[b]同一关卡平行boss战力差距过大[/b]，三头犬‎‎>>双子，世界蛇>>谜语人，见boss输一半绝非虚言。 2.[b]boss、boss招式、小怪无法同时处理让玩家疲于奔命[/b]，玩家一边应对boss招式的同时一边还要应付小怪，一边还要想方设法削减boss血量，发牌不好DPS上不去的时候只能将战线拉长，小怪和boss招式还会随时间而增强，最终只能在糊成一坨或是叠在一起的一堆词汇的侵袭下慢性死亡。你要么boss加强一下然后boss出来后不再出怪，要么给boss减少攻击方式做机制消掉技能生成物能削减血量，即当又立的设计只能造就粪怪，让人厌烦。 3.[b]部分敌人的设计与构筑无关[/b]，点名世界蛇和诗人。我通过肉鸽系统获得的构筑好坏，与我对boss的对策毫无关系！世界蛇刚需打出对应字符造成伤害，并且会生成必须打出字符才能消除的生成物；诗人则是要求玩家打出一首诗，并且会为小怪添加“双倍输入”的buff。玩家辛辛苦苦做了一整轮的构筑，你关底boss让我滚回去老老实实打字?就像你花了一周改了十版的文档，结果甲方一拍板说用第一版，这对肉鸽游戏而言简直就是灾难。 总而言之，如果你希望在这个游戏里混的如鱼得水，你必须要是打字高手，同时也要慢慢学着成为肉鸽高手。二者缺一，你都无法通过这场对受众残酷的筛选。或许从成就系统中就能看出这个令人啼笑皆非的事实：作为发售一年半的作品，初始武器的通关成就仅有30%的人获得，68个成就中甚至只有两个有超过10%的获得率。如此病态的数据还未让制作者警醒? 究竟是傲慢还是摆烂，恐怕不得而知。 [h2]2.作为游戏的深度是几乎没有的，数值像是用脚填的[/h2] [strike]前面写太多了人有点累，不想行文直接分点来写了。[/strike] 1.真的可以说是可怜到一眼都能看到头的构筑深度。主武器+四个副武器的设定外加除了少数特殊强化外全是纯粹的数值提升锁死了构筑上限，局内拿啥基本上全看局外选了啥、哪个强以及他给发啥，不同武器间仅有分大类的无聊透顶的强化联动，没有化学反应般的技能组合，更没有多物品组合的质变设计。 2.让人忍俊不禁的平衡性。猎手超模，利刃还行，什么屠夫、幽灵啥的⋯⋯别逗我笑。我都懒得分析了，游戏自带DPS显示，那随便选选就几十DPS的和养半天查无此人的泾渭分明。 3.数值成长比老奶奶拿烂泥糊的墙还要粗糙。我攻击力加成是10%/20%/30%，攻速加成是10%/20%/30%，诶范围加成还是10%/20%/30%，持续时间加成依旧是10%/20%/30%；无人机是10%/20%/30%，炮塔是10%/20%/30%，主武器还TMD是10%/20%/30%?我玩第一把看见这个数值直接眼神都清澈了，你一个肉鸽游戏数值哪能做的这么糙的啊，你做个游戏都不vba拉个表投个骰看看你引以为傲的不同10%/20%/30%之间对战力的提升到底有多大差距?_? 4.你的局外金币获取像是在希望玩家全都玩几十上百个小时，然而你的平均游戏时长仅有4.4h[i]（数据来源：小黑盒）[/i]，90%+的玩家都被难度吓跑了。 5.我说对单主武器就该设计为秒杀。打字基础收益=主武器攻击+副武器生成。由大多数主武器的对单特性，必须保证副武器有足够的练度来清理顾及不到的敌人，随着关卡进程的推进，主武器自身能起到的作用会越来越低，打字基础收益→副武器生成，而副武器生成与字符有关，此时有些词汇的打出变得毫无意义，因此我认为对单主武器的秒杀机制是必要的（当然可以有敌人拥有多个血条，需要多次击中）。 6.武器机制略有单一，伤害偏多，偶有控制，花活偏少。说白了就是不够“好玩”。武器本身就来来回回那么几个，能玩的套路也就武器自身伤害、状态、暴击等寥寥几种。多设计一些例如弹射（碰到边界反弹且加速的碰撞无人机）、分裂（击中敌人分裂的无人机）、频闪（完成词汇时对全屏造成基于该词汇字符数的基础伤害）、黑洞（生成后持续吸附敌人到某区域并使区域中敌人所需字符统一）、铁锁（链接多个敌人共享所受伤害的炮塔）、提词器（错拼时，消耗能量来完成拼写）、光环（能够减速推开敌人）等特殊机制，使游戏从画圈比大小的设计思路中脱离开来，才能使玩家玩的更有乐趣。 [h2]总评：亟待打磨的肉鸽打字模拟器[/h2] +++[b]优秀的创意玩法[/b] ++[b]寓教于乐的打字练习[/b] +[b]简约清爽的画面[/b] +[b]动感的音效[/b] –––[b]打字门槛埋没肉鸽玩法[/b] –[b]缺少缓冲设计[/b] –[b]成长系统缺乏深度[/b] –[b]粗旷的数值设计[/b] –[b]武器平衡一言难尽[/b]

The game is enjoyable at times, but it has its flaws. There are moments when the keyboard stops responding, and to be honest, I suspect this is intentional. I’ve exited the game only to find that the keyboard works fine outside of it. It honestly feels like the game is cheating. The boss levels are designed to be difficult, not because you’re required to type quickly, but because the words are stacked on top of each other, making it nearly impossible to decipher what you’re supposed to type. You end up either taking multiple hits or simply skipping over those chaotic blocks of text. I understand the goal is to improve typing speed, but if that’s the case, this game falls short. It often feels like it’s trying to slow you down or make your typing seem unreliable. I know I can type faster—I'm able to type 110 words per minute daily at work. But in this game, I find myself typing a word one letter at a time, and it still doesn’t register correctly. The challenges and levels are thrown at you so quickly and messily that distinguishing one word from another becomes nearly impossible. Eventually, it just becomes frustrating. The only redeeming factor is that, when on sale, the game might be considered a somewhat fair buy. However, aside from that, there are far better typing games out there. Honestly, the game is fun but I thought the metaprogression would be more in depth. The game has such a high typing speed threshold but the lack of metaprogression makes it hard to keep up with. You choose 2 augments to take with you (1 or 2 more if you're lucky enough to get to the higher difficulties) and that's it. No stat boosts to help you do more damage, no slot unlocks to mix and match augments, etc. If everything were unlocked from the start, it'd be one thing but having such a poorly implemented progression system makes the game feel unrewarding and a waste of time. If you have the fortitude to grind out all the coins required to unlock the augments, you still wouldn't be able to progress to the higher difficulties as just difficulty 3/6 requires at minimum a 120+ wpm just to beat. Also, there are no true modifiers to alter your runs and with the lack of content available, the game feels repetitive after just a few runs.

I'm incredibly disappointed that this game has no learning features. It starts off by assuming that you know how to type at an intermediate level. Its otherwise exactly what I would have wanted out of a typing game. If the dev can incorporate a learning based progression system into the game, my opinion instantly changes. As it stands, avoid the game if you aren't good at typing properly. otherwise you are likely to reinforce whatever bad habits you may already have.

Definitely the best typing game that I've played on steam. The rouge-like format keeps you coming back to play far more consistently than other typing games, and run's usually last from 10-30 mins at approx 100 WPM. That said, I would appreciate more tailored difficulty options so I can tweak the settings to actually support better typing habits. I find that during highly frenetic sequences I begin to prioritize speed over accuracy, and I think adding more options to incentivize and reward you for accuracy and punish mistypes would be a huge improvement in terms of ensuring the game actually helps improve typing performance over time. 'Slow is smooth and smooth is fast' is a better principle to be internalizing to actually boost WPM than 'spam my keyboard and hope I don't mess up' -- which tends to be the natural response when difficulty ramps up as quickly as it does in many of these modes. It's not that I need the game to be way way slower -- it's more so an issue of misaligned incentives based on how the game's default mechanics work, as there aren't huge penalties for mistyping and there aren't super significant benefits to accurate typing unless you get lucky and select specific perks.

This scratched the same itch as Typer Shark did. What I find really interesting about it, though, is that typing quickly isn't enough to get you through levels. As someone who has a 100+ WPM, it can be easy to outstrip the pacing of a lot of typing games and get bored. This game truly rewards synergistic builds rather than those builds just feeling like a "win more" option. The simplistic presentation makes it very readable as a player, so I never feel like I'm losing just because I couldn't tell what was going on in the screen quickly enough.
